newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: PRESS DIGEST - S.Korean newspapers - Jan 7
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - S.Korean newspapers - Jan 7

text.p: The following is a summary of major South Korean political stories in leading newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Seoul. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not gaurantee their accuracy. Telephone: (822) 727-5650. Fax: (822) 727-5666.

- After unions resumed all-out strikes on Monday, tensions were on the rise as the government took steps to summon union leaders for questioning. The business world also declared it would take strong counter-measures against the unions themselves.

- Despite government guidelines to restrict increases in college tuition fees to within five percent, most universities have raised the fees above 10 percent, some going as high as 19. The Ministry of Education said it would reduce financial support for those universities that have refused to meet the guidelines.

- The Korean Confederation of Trade Unions (KCTU) warned that if the government attempted to use force or arrest strike leaders, groups which had postponed strikes indefinitely, such as the subway and Korea Telecom unions, would immediately join the industrial action.

- The government announced that it expects a low growth rate this year of nearly five percent, as efforts to control rising inflation and reduce the trade deficit will be emphasized in order to focus on the economy.
